question: With an identical takeoff and physical handback, can rolling continuous exit planning improve completion? Does a larger approach family still add recoverable cases under that stronger exit?
baseline: original three exits, fixed clearance and common default. Fixed gate entry and unfiltered straight/gate-action are extra same-state controls.
primary: For each root and gate, one approach selected in hindsight based on average over the three hidden pushes. Report as finite-family potential. Also report deployed gate-rule paired old/rolling and physical losses and rescues.
grouping: Paired by root, stratified by the two fixed maps. Report gate side, section, pushes and whole-task and collision denominators.

acceptance.pre: D-B >=5pp and net rescues across multiple roots on shared-force rule. Mark inconclusive when paired intervals and effects across maps or sides do not support a direction.
acceptance.post: If B-A >=5pp but D-B small, prioritize post-lock planning. Check fixed gate paired results and collisions before choosing method.
acceptance.admission: When old entries and physical exits suffice but scoring loses, compare correcting admission under held-out calibration.
acceptance.limits: Directional screen. No guaranteed success, continuous optimality or independence across branch replicas.

scope_latency: Saved DEV state resident on device through publication or rejection. Report observation extraction and first subsequent real controller consumption separately when available.
stop: Stop at four paired batches and analysis, or record a technical failure for repair. No replacement maps, data-dependent expansion or training in P0-B.
